passage:
Himani,
I'm writing this because you were asleep when I got in, and you turned away when I said good morning.
Yesterday at six I was in the budget meeting, and Pallavi called three times. When I stepped out, she said she'd fainted at work and was alone at the clinic. I texted you 'will be late, don't wait' with one thumb while the meeting carried on behind me. I meant to send a second message. I didn't. I forgot. I sat with Pallavi until her brother arrived at eleven.
I read my text again this morning. It sounds like I didn't think of you at all. I did. I just didn't say it. I know you'd had a long day too, and it isn't the first time I've gone quiet on you.
Your husband,
Kunal

qa.q: Until when did Kunal sit with Pallavi?
qa.a: He sat with Pallavi until her brother arrived at eleven.

qa.q: What did Kunal realise when he reread his text in the morning?
qa.a: He saw that its bare words made it look as if he hadn't thought of Himani at all, and he seems sorry and worried.

qa.q: What could Kunal do differently in a busy moment like that?
qa.a: Add a few words of context, like 'friend unwell, will explain', or send the second message as soon as he stepped out, so Himani isn't left guessing.

qa.q: How might Himani have felt receiving 'will be late, don't wait'?
qa.a: Tired from her own day, she likely read it as one more sign she didn't matter, which is why she turned away in the morning.

passage:
You're asking what happened last Thursday? It's silly, really. I was in a client meeting that ran over. Then Afreen, my old college friend, messaged that she'd fainted at work and was alone at the clinic.
So I texted my wife, Vasudha, under the table: "will be late, don't wait." I was thinking of five things at once. I didn't mention Afreen. I didn't even put a heart or anything.
I got home at eleven. Vasudha was on the sofa with the TV off. She said, "Of course you were late," and went to bed. I'm Nikhil, her husband of two years, and I stood there holding my keys, thinking, what did I do? Only later I saw my message the way she did, after her own twelve-hour day.

qa.q: Where was Afreen when she messaged?
qa.a: Alone at the clinic, after fainting at work.

qa.q: What was Nikhil feeling as he stood holding his keys?
qa.a: He felt confused and uneasy, not yet understanding why Vasudha was upset.

qa.q: What small change to his text could have prevented this?
qa.a: Adding one line, such as "Afreen's unwell, taking her to the clinic", so Vasudha knew why he was late.

qa.q: What is it like for Vasudha to get the text after her twelve-hour day?
qa.a: She likely felt tired and unimportant, reading it as another late night without explanation.

grounding: Shows a husband sending a terse text during a busy meeting, forgetting to explain a friend is unwell, and his tired wife feeling unimportant.

subtype: Stage 1: A terse message in a busy hour [Actor]
passage: "Sit, beta, since you're typing so fast on that phone. Let me tell you something from when your chachi and I were newly married, twenty years back.
